title: Ayush Thakur
text:
I build and evaluate AI systems.
I am a Manager, AI Engineering at Weights & Biases by CoreWeave. I work on internal coding agents, harness benchmarks, memory, and methods for learning from previous runs.
Previously, I was a growth MLE at W&B. I built open-source integrations, production RAG systems such as Wandbot, technical courses, and practical ML writing. This work helped developers adopt W&B across training, evaluation, and LLM application workflows.
I started with autonomous robots and computer vision. Those projects taught me to work quickly, test ideas in hardware and code, and own the result. I am looking for research collaborators working on agents, memory, and learning from experience.

title: Work

LLM systems and evaluation


2024Production RAG


Wandbot: an evaluation-driven refactorReworked W&B’s open-source documentation assistant around systematic evaluation. Answer accuracy rose from 72% to 81%, latency fell by 84%, and a full evaluation run went from roughly two hours to under ten minutes. Nearly 50 experiments made the trade-offs between quality, speed, and cost visible.Read the case study · SourceRAGEvaluationProduction




2023LLM evaluation


Evaluating, comparing, and optimizing LLM systemsBuilt a workflow for comparing system configurations with human labels, LLM judges, retrieval metrics, and parameter search.Technical reportLLMOpsEvals

LlamaIndex × W&BBuilt W&B instrumentation for retrieval and LLM traces, debugging query pipelines, and versioning indexes and embeddings.WalkthroughLlamaIndexTracing

title: About
text:
How I work
I prefer work with a short path from question to evidence. I build an initial version, instrument it, inspect failures, and decide what to change. Writing is part of that process: it forces me to state what I observed and makes the result reusable.

title: About
text:
The “Enginear” story
When I was ten, a teacher asked what I wanted to become. I said “engineer.” Asked to spell it, I got it wrong, and was told that someone who could not spell the word could not become one.
I kept the misspelling—Enginear—as the name of this site.
